audit_findings.title: FSA shares are counted without the matching cash proceeds
audit_findings.magnitude: Approximately $899.4 million of June 30, 2026 physical-settlement proceeds for 7.479798 million outstanding FSA shares; approximately $14.07 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation includes physically settleable FSA shares in the diluted-share denominator but omits the corresponding proceeds from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, IDACORP could have settled the FSAs with physical delivery of 5,180,180 shares of common stock to the counterparties in exchange for cash of $ 560.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated numerator-denominator mismatch. Adding approximately $899.4 million to the base equity value would increase value from $45.89 to approximately $59.96 per share before considering later settlements. That is a roughly 31% change in base value and is material even though the result remains below the $135.70 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct shares and proceeds at September 5, 2026 agreement by agreement. Rerun all scenarios using either physical-settlement shares plus proceeds or the applicable net-share settlement dilution, including the July 2026 settlement.

audit_findings.title: A definitive Oregon divestiture is missing from the perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $154 million base purchase price; $120.497 million net held-for-sale carrying amount at June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The sale changes the operating-earnings perimeter and, if completed, adds transaction proceeds to the equity bridge while removing the Oregon operations and assets from forecast owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: On February 13, 2026, Idaho Power executed a definitive agreement to sell its Oregon electric distribution business as well as certain Oregon transmission assets to OTEC.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the latest filing classifies $129.667 million of assets and $9.170 million of liabilities as held for sale and expects completion within one year. The gross proceeds equal about 5.3% of the $2.933 billion base equity value, but the net value direction remains mixed because the valuation also must remove Oregon earnings and account for adjustments, costs, taxes, and closing risk.
audit_findings.action: Confirm transaction status as of September 5, 2026 and rerun the valuation with probability-weighted net proceeds, taxes and transaction costs, and Oregon earnings and assets removed from every historical and forecast period.

audit_findings.title: AFUDC may be counted as current owner earnings despite being noncash financing accrual
audit_findings.magnitude: $98.700 million pretax in 2025, comprising $62.489 million of equity AFUDC and $36.211 million of borrowed-funds AFUDC
audit_findings.mechanism: Unremoved AFUDC increases historical owner earnings and the trend anchor even though the associated cash return is generally recovered later through rates; future rate-base earnings could then be counted again.
audit_findings.evidence: With one exception, for the HCC relicensing project, cash is not realized currently from such allowance; it is realized under the ratemaking process over the service life of the related property through increased revenues resulting from a higher rate base and higher depreciation expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that AFUDC is generally not current cash and that its 2025 amount was large. It does not establish whether the owner-earnings bridges already remove or offset both components. If they do not, the potential distortion is large relative to the $214.3 million anchor and could materially change the DCF.
audit_findings.action: Trace equity and borrowed-funds AFUDC separately through every annual OE bridge, identify any offset within capital expenditures or cash-flow adjustments, remove any net current-period benefit, and rerun the trend, anchor, and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Finite ADITC amortization may be embedded as durable earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $40.3 million in 2025, equal to 18.3% of 2025 OE; $167.8 million remained available at December 31, 2025
audit_findings.mechanism: Accelerated ADITC amortization reduces tax expense and increases reported earnings; if retained in historical OE, it can raise the trend anchor and terminal earnings assigned to a finite regulatory credit pool.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, Idaho Power recorded amortization of $ 40.3 million of ADITC.
audit_findings.explanation: The finite benefit and its scale are demonstrated, but its inclusion in the supplied OE series is unresolved. The 2025 amount alone is material relative to $219.7 million of OE, and the remaining pool does not support treating that benefit as perpetual without an explicit normalization.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile ADITC amortization and related cash-flow adjustments for every OE year, remove any net finite benefit from sustainable OE, and recompute the log trend, anchor, and valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Static shares may overstate per-share growth during a capital-funded expansion
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF grows aggregate OE while holding shares at 63.910353 million; future equity issued to finance the $6.3-$7.2 billion capital program would dilute the OE and value attributable to each current share.
audit_findings.evidence: Idaho Power's estimate of capital expenditures from 2026 to 2030 is in the range of $6.3 billion to $7.2 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking financing risk rather than a demonstrated error in historical OE. The filing establishes a large capital program, an approximately 50/50 target capital structure, outstanding equity programs, and contemplated further issuance, but it does not establish the amount, timing, or price of future shares or how much capital will be funded from retained earnings.
audit_findings.action: Build annual funding schedules through the explicit forecast, including retained earnings, debt, settled FSAs, ATM capacity, and additional equity issuance, then rerun value per share or document that each scenario's growth rate is already net of dilution.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease capital cost may disappear from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.762 million of 2025 principal payments; $226.618 million initial ROU asset and $222.856 million lease liability present value
audit_findings.mechanism: If ROU amortization is added back while the noncash asset addition and financing-classified principal payments are excluded, OE omits the capital charge for obtaining the battery asset while retaining only lease interest.
audit_findings.evidence: Amortization of the lease ROU asset is included in depreciation and amortization, and the interest expense associated with the finance lease liabilities is included in interest on long-term debt and finance leases on the consolidated statements of income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the lease amounts and cash-flow classification, but the supplied record does not show how the OE bridge treats ROU amortization, lease principal, or regulatory recovery. The 2025 principal amount is only about 1.8% of the $214.3 million anchor, but the 20-year liability makes the continuing and terminal effect potentially larger and presently unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease amortization, principal payments, ROU additions, and PCA recovery through the OE calculation; deduct principal or an equivalent recurring capital charge without double-counting interest, then rerun the anchor and DCF if a net omission exists.
